Patient Safety Indicators

Patient safety indicators — what they are, common indicators and how nurses improve them.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define patient safety indicators
  • List common patient safety indicators
  • Describe how nurses improve safety indicators

In simple words

Patient safety indicators are measures that show how safely care is delivered. They track events like falls, infections, medication errors and pressure ulcers. Hospitals use them to find problems and improve care.

Nurses collect data and act daily to keep indicator rates low.

Common patient safety indicators

Indicator What it measures
Fall rate Patients who fall per 1,000 patient days
HAI rate Hospital-acquired infections (CAUTI, CLABSI, VAP, SSI)
Medication error rate Errors in prescribing, dispensing, administering
Pressure ulcer rate New pressure ulcers during stay
Readmission rate Patients readmitted soon after discharge

How nurses improve indicators

  • Follow standard precautions and hand hygiene to reduce HAIs.
  • Assess fall risk and assist mobility to reduce falls.
  • Follow the five rights of medication to reduce errors.
  • Turn patients every 2 hours and assess skin to reduce pressure ulcers.
  • Document accurately so data reflects real care.

🔴 Indicators drive improvement

Patient safety indicators show where care needs improvement. Nurses’ daily actions directly affect these rates.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Hand hygiene and asepsis — reduce HAI rates.
  • Fall risk assessment — use a fall scale; assist mobility; keep call bell within reach.
  • Medication safety — five rights; double-check high-risk drugs.
  • Pressure ulcer prevention — 2-hourly turning, skin assessment, pressure-relieving surfaces.
  • Accurate documentation — records the true picture for indicator reporting.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Patient safety indicators measure how safely care is delivered.
  2. Indicators: fall rate, HAI rate, medication error rate, pressure ulcer rate, readmission rate.
  3. Nurses reduce HAIs with hand hygiene and asepsis.
  4. Nurses reduce falls with risk assessment and mobility assistance.
  5. Accurate documentation keeps indicator data truthful.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. HAIs include CAUTI, CLABSI, VAP and SSI.
  2. Medication errors are reduced by the five rights.
  3. Pressure ulcers are reduced by 2-hourly turning and skin assessment.
  4. Readmission rates show whether discharge planning worked.

📌 Memory trick

Safety indicators: “F-H-M-P-R” — Falls, HAIs, Medication errors, Pressure ulcers, Readmissions.

60-second revision

  • Safety indicators = measures of how safely care is delivered.
  • Falls, HAIs, medication errors, pressure ulcers, readmissions.
  • Nurses reduce rates with hand hygiene, fall risk, five rights, turning.
  • Document accurately.
  • Indicators drive quality improvement.

Test yourself

A patient safety indicator measures:

Answer: B. Patient safety indicators measure how safely care is delivered and where improvement is needed.

HAI rate measures:

Answer: B. HAI rate measures hospital-acquired infections such as CAUTI, CLABSI, VAP and SSI.

Nurses reduce medication errors by:

Answer: B. Following the five rights of medication administration reduces errors.

Pressure ulcer rate is reduced by:

Answer: A. Regular turning (every 2 hours) and skin assessment reduce pressure ulcers.

Accurate documentation matters because:

Answer: B. Accurate records reflect the care actually given, so safety indicator data is truthful.
